item.title: Topic Overview
item.description: Spiking Neural Networks Spiking Neural Networks, or SNNs, are neural networks that compute with events.

item.title: Spiking Neural Networks
item.description: Spiking Neural Networks Learners will understand how spiking neural networks compute with event-driven spikes, why they are compared against conventional neural networks, how major SNN training strategies differ, and how to interpret accuracy, latency, energy, spike count, and convergence tradeoffs ...

item.title: 1. Why This Topic Exists and the Mechanism Works
item.description: 1. Why This Topic Exists and the Mechanism Works Build up why this topic exists and the mechanism works one step at a time.

item.title: 1.1 Why Spiking Neural Networks Exist
item.description: Why Spiking Neural Networks Exist Imagine a small camera watching a quiet hallway.

item.title: 1.2 Asynchronous Brain-Inspired Computation
item.description: A spike event already gives us a different way to imagine computation: instead of every neuron continuously sending a changing number forward, a neuron can stay quiet until it has something to report.

item.title: 1.3 Sparse Events and Energy Efficiency
item.description: Sparse Events and Energy Efficiency Imagine the spike event from the previous idea as a tiny message sent through a network: a neuron stays quiet while its input is too weak, then emits a brief spike when its internal state reaches a firing threshold.

item.title: 1.4 The Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron
item.description: The Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron Once information is carried by spike events, a neuron needs a simple rule for deciding when an event should happen.

item.title: 1.5 Encoding, Excitation, and Lateral Inhibition
item.description: Encoding, Excitation, and Lateral Inhibition You have already seen how a spiking neuron can sit quietly while incoming spikes push its internal state upward, then fire when enough evidence has accumulated to cross a threshold.
